hiragana.note: Small っ doesn't have its own sound. It marks a brief pause that doubles the consonant right after it — かた (kata) vs かった (katta).

katakana.note: Small ッ works exactly like hiragana っ: it doubles the consonant that follows it, e.g. ベッド (beddo).
ー stretches the vowel sound right before it. コーヒー is koohii (kōhī), not kohi.
